pr_title: fix(compiler): normalize line endings in ICU expansions
pr_body:
The html parser already normalizes line endings (converting
`\r\n` to `\n`) for most text in templates but it was missing
the expressions of ICU expansions.

In ViewEngine backticked literal strings used to define inline
templates were already normalized by the TypeScript parser.
In Ivy we are parsing the raw text of the source file directly so
the line ending need to be manually normalized.

This change in behaviour was causing the computed i18n message
id for ICUs to change depending upon the current line ending settings
of the environment extracting or merging translations.

Closes #36725


----


Capturing the warning message content here:

When parsing an external template file "TestComp" one or more ICU expressions were found that contain `\\r\\n` line-endings.
These would have been normalized to `\\n` but this would change the computed id for their i18n messages.
The line endings were left unnormalized for backward compatibility on this occasion.
In a future release, these line endings will be normalized, which will be a breaking change.
It is suggested that you try opting into this behavior now to see what effect it will have on your message ids by setting `"i18nNormalizeExternalTemplateLineEndingsInICUs": true` in the `angularCompilerOptions` of `tsconfig.json`
The ICU expressions that need normalizing are:
pr_comments:
It turns out that things are really broken as they stand, but that also means that this would be a breaking change for a specific scenario...

On a machine where line endings are set to be `\r\n`, there is a difference between inline and external templates. TypeScript will normalise line endings in backtick string literals to be `\n`. So in ViewEngine the line ending doesn't matter. But in external templates (i.e. `templateUrl`) TypeScript does not get a look in, and we process the contents of the file directly, which means that the line endings are taken into account.

As shown in this PR, the only thing that is affected is the ICU `expression` string - the rest of ICUs and in fact the rest of templates already have the line endings normalised when we parse templates.

This is quite broken, right now, since two people working on different machines with different line ending settings would generate different message ids for the same external templates.

The right thing to do is to fix this but then Windows users with `\r\n` line endings in their external templates will find that their ICU message IDs have changed.
I added a fixup commit that should make this change non-breaking - and provides a opt-in switch that we can flip in the future.
Marked as `master-only` because it touches the public API (of the compiler options).

Something that came to mind: if there's a lot of components for which a warning is generated, the compilation will generate a lot of long warning messages. Maybe we can find a way to accumulate all occurrences and log them once.

> Something that came to mind: if there's a lot of components for which a warning is generated, the compilation will generate a lot of long warning messages. Maybe we can find a way to accumulate all occurrences and log them once.

Actually thinking about it, this is a significant issue. There is no straightforward way to aggregate these warnings without making the compiler know more than it ought to about how the warning is structured...

* I wonder if we could hide this warning behind a verbose option?
* Or perhaps post a simple one line warning and write some documentation for it? Perhaps a link to this PR?
* Or perhaps for now we should just not display the warning?
I decided to go with not writing any warning to the console at this stage. Apart from anything, this does not really play nice with CLI integration.

@IgorMinar can you clarify what you mean by:

> Let's see if we can consider using a default value in the public API instead of undefined.

> Now that no warning is being generated, this should be fine to go into patch once again.

@JoostK - the `master-only` label is due to the public API change, not because of the warning.

> > Let's see if we can consider using a default value in the public API instead of undefined.

So I think we have found the source[sic] of the problem. Traditionally we have had to keep whitespace inside ICU expressions when generating message ids. But it seems that we should be normalizing out the `\r` characters from line-endings. At least it appears that the old ViewEngine message extraction is doing so.

By the way, if you were to use `XLIFF 2` or `XMB` formats for your translation files then this is already fixed. Note that the "decimal" ids are the same in both cases. The `XLIFF 1.2` format is using a legacy message id digest that we want to retire.
Ok this makes sense.  Thanks for taking a look into it!
Tracking internally as FW-2101

I did some more digging. This is down to how we (and TypeScript) handles line endings in backticked strings.  In the TypeScript `scanTemplateAndSetTokenValue()` function, which is responsible for dealing with such backticked strings there is this comment:

```
// Speculated ECMAScript 6 Spec 11.8.6.1:
// <CR><LF> and <CR> LineTerminatorSequences are normalized to <LF> for Template Values
```

And then they go ahead and nornalize the line endings in the backticked strings.
You can see this on their AST tokens, which have `text` and `rawText` properties. The former only has `\n` while the latter can include `\r\n`.

In the ivy compiler we do our own tokenizing of the template string, where there is some normalization of line endings... https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/458dc10ddc85acdaffe3c876bf1a4fc1142092b2/packages/compiler/src/ml_parser/lexer.ts#L169-L178 ...but I think we need to ensure it happens for ICUs too...
